text:
Nashville won because of one period and one goalie. Miro Heiskanen put Dallas ahead 47 seconds in, but the Predators answered with two power-play goals in the first, Steven Stamkos snapping one home at 4:46 and Nils Hoglander deflecting in the winner at 15:49 on a 4% chance. NSH went 2 for 3 with the man advantage while DAL went 0 for 1, and that gap decided a game the Stars controlled for long stretches afterward.

The first period was the Predators' only real stretch of control, 1.33 expected goals to 0.59. After that the chances flipped. DAL outchanced NSH 0.89 to 0.52 in the second and 0.89 to 0.32 in the third, and finished with 65 shot attempts to 52 and 30 shots on goal to 26. The model gave DAL a 54% chance of deserving the win to NSH's 46%, and at even strength the teams were level at 1.83 expected goals for NSH and 1.82 for DAL.

Juuse Saros made the difference. He stopped 29 of 30 and saved 1.37 goals more than the shots deserved, including Roope Hintz's 26% look in the second period, the best chance of the night that didn't go in. Casey DeSmith stopped 24 of 26 at the other end and was roughly even with expectation. Stamkos, Saros and Ryan O'Reilly took the three stars.
